pr_title: dts: bindings: Fix NXP USB bindings
pr_body:
NXP USB bindings were combined into one binding and using a property corresponding to HAL enums which is improper use of devicetree. This PR takes an approach that is uglier in the driver but that is more in line with how DT should be used. 

Fixes #50506.

issue_context.title: nxp,mcux-usbd devicetree binding issues
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

The point of a  devicetree binding is to describe hardware and its initial configuration. We have carved out a few exceptions for driver-specific property names prefixed with `zephyr,`. However, we should not be designing devicetree bindings to cater to the software requirements of vendor HALs.

This USB device driver binding has a name that seems to specifically refer to the HAL itself, not the actual hardware. It also has problematic properties, such as `usb-controller-index`, added in 3a7c719fb45ea33f35a6464c8bbaa736ab6fc8cb.

**Expected behavior**

Devicetree bindings that reflect the hardware, not the software. Removal of this binding and replacement with individual bindings for the IP blocks in question, as many as needed. Removal of HAL-specific configuration properties.
comments: @mbolivar-nordic. I am looking to address this change as part of an updated MCUX USB driver that would use the new USB framework.

review_comments:
I'm assuming you are absolutely sure it will always only ever be one or the other. If so, feel free to resolve this comment.

If not, can you add a BUILD_ASSERT that the devicetree does not have nodes with both compatibles in it, just to document the assumption?

Something like `BUILD_ASSERT(DT_NUM_INST_STATUS_OKAY(nxp_lpcip3511) + DT_NUM_INST_STATUS_OKAY(nxp_ehci), ...)`.

For this SOC specific section- could we use an approach like this?

```
/* LPC3511 IP */
#ifdef CONFIG_USB_DC_NXP_LPCIP3511
#if DT_INST_ENUM_HAS_VALUE(0, maximum_speed, high_speed)
#define CONTROLLER_ID kUSB_ControllerLpcIp3511Hs0
#else
#define CONTROLLER_ID kUSB_ControllerLpcIp3511Hs0
#endif

/* EHCI IP */
#ifdef CONFIG_USB_DC_NXP_EHCI
#define CONTROLLER_ID kUSB_ControllerEhci##DT_INST_PROP(0, index)
#endif
```
Not sure what your thoughts on this are

Introducing an index property defeats the purpose of solving the issue linked since we are once again putting things in DT to satisfy HAL enum names. Also we had a similar discussion on S32 PRs before and decided to avoid putting index numbers in DT to satisfy HAL arrays.

It is a good idea but there is no guarantee that this pattern holds for future SOCs so I don't see the advantage of making this over-complicated. I would rather maintain just this list of things per SOC rather than do these gymnastics with every new great idea for an api change the HAL comes up with for every new release. For example, there could be an SOC with two instances of LPC3511 which this doesn't account for because there might be a case where only the index 1 is enabled by the zephyr user. And there could be an SOC where the HAL adds yet another random name of the array like they have already done with USBHS_STACK_BASE_ADDRS vs USBHS_BASE_ADDRS. And sometimes the HAL puts a random 0 in the first index of USB_BASE_ADDRS which would break things. I don't think having the SOC ifdefs is really adding any more technical debt than this PR is solving, someone enabling USB on an SOC already currently has to figure out which hal enum corresponds to the modules on the chip, the only difference is now putting it in this driver file instead of the devicetree. And that will be obvious because of the error, the same as getting a DTC error before for not putting the controller enum property.

If we really want a better solution it has to come from the SDK itself is my opinion. Either that or make the driver zephyr native as the usb_dc_kinetis is, but both of those things are outside the scope of this PR which is just a quick fix of the abuse of devicetree.

I have said why I disagree and my opinion has not changed. Additionally, you are proposing runtime overhead for something that can be determined at compile time. And as you are pointing out, trying to make this more and more generic just leads to more and more runtime overhead. I don't think there is any point to attempt to optimize this here with these complications when we know the most optimal solution is going to come from the SDK and remove the need from any of this. I'm not changing this in the PR. The scope is fixing devicetree, not doing gymnastics with the SDK definitions.
Understood. At the end of the day, this fixes the issue. I don't particularly like the approach, but I'm not going to block over it.
